## Question 31 — Industrial Chemistry (25 marks)

**(a)** (i) Write an equation using structural formulae to describe saponification. Use ethyl propanoate as one of the reactants. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

(ii) Describe a procedure that can be used to carry out saponification and test the product in a school laboratory. **(3 marks)**

\vspace{6cm}

**(b)** The Contact process for the production of sulfuric acid includes a step whereby sulfur dioxide is converted to sulfur trioxide in an equilibrium reaction:

$$\ce{SO2(g) + 1/2 O2(g) <=> SO3(g)} \quad \Delta H = -99 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

\ce{SO2} and \ce{O2} were added to a closed container. The production of \ce{SO3} over time is shown on the graph below.

(i) Copy the graph below into your answer booklet and sketch a second curve on the same axes to demonstrate the production of \ce{SO3} over time when the reaction is repeated at a higher temperature. Clearly label the two curves. **(2 marks)**

![Graph of SO3 concentration vs time](images/q31b-graph.png){width=60%}

(ii) At a certain temperature, the equilibrium constant, K, is 12.1 for this reaction as written in the equation above.

At the same temperature, 1.0 mol \ce{SO2} and 1.0 mol \ce{O2} were added to a 1.0 litre closed container. At a point in time, the concentration of \ce{SO3} in the container was measured as 0.70 mol L^-1^.

Had equilibrium been reached in the container at this point? Use calculations to justify your answer. **(4 marks)**

\vspace{10cm}

\newpage

**(c)** The raw materials required to produce sodium carbonate by the Solvay process are limestone and brine. Part of the process is represented by the flow chart.

![Solvay process flow chart](images/q31c-flowchart.png){width=80%}

(i) Name the products labelled X and Y. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{2cm}

(ii) How is the brine purified? Include a relevant chemical equation in your answer. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

(iii) Explain the role of ammonia in the manufacture of sodium carbonate. Include relevant chemical equation(s) in your answer. **(3 marks)**

\vspace{6cm}

**(d)** Assess the extent to which technological advances have overcome the technical and environmental issues associated with the industrial production of sodium hydroxide. **(7 marks)**

\vspace{15cm}

## Question 32 — Shipwrecks, Corrosion and Conservation (25 marks)

**(a)** A first-hand investigation is to be carried out to compare the rate of corrosion of metals in acidic and neutral solutions.

(i) Outline a suitable procedure for this investigation. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

(ii) Explain the expected result. Include relevant half equations in your answer. **(3 marks)**

\vspace{6cm}

**(b)** (i) Outline TWO different ways to increase the rate of an electrolysis reaction. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

(ii) When two carbon electrodes were placed in a blue, 3 mol L^-1^ solution of \ce{CuCl2} and connected to a 6 V DC power supply, bubbles started appearing at the anode. After some time, the mass of the cathode had increased and the intensity of the blue colour had decreased.

Account for these observations. Include relevant chemical equations in your answer. **(4 marks)**

\vspace{8cm}

\newpage

**(c)** In 1912, the ship *Titanic* sank in water over 3 km deep. The wreck was discovered in 1985.

(i) Why did scientists predict that the rate of corrosion would have been slow at this depth? **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

(ii) Explain why extra precautions need to be taken when retrieving wooden artefacts from sea water compared to fresh water. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

(iii) Describe how electrolysis can be used to remove chloride ions from a metallic artefact. Support your answer with a labelled diagram. **(3 marks)**

\vspace{8cm}

**(d)** Analyse the effect that the work of Volta and Davy had in reducing corrosion of ocean-going vessels. **(7 marks)**

\vspace{15cm}

## Question 35 — Forensic Chemistry (25 marks)

**(a)** (i) Outline a test that could be carried out in a school laboratory to distinguish between sodium carbonate and starch. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

(ii) The emission spectrum of sodium is shown.

![Sodium emission spectrum](images/q35a-emission-spectrum.png){width=80%}

\vspace{6cm}

**(b)** (i) A group of students tried to use chromatography to separate the pigments extracted from a plant leaf. They put a small spot of the pigments on a strip of paper and drew a line across the paper to show the starting point. They then allowed solvent to run up the paper.

Explain why a pencil rather than a pen should be used to draw the line. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{4cm}

(ii) The students then tried to use chromatography to separate an alkanol and an alkanoic acid. They found that the spot of the alkanol and alkanoic acid mixture did not move when an alkane was used as the solvent.

\vspace{8cm}

\vspace{8cm}
